questions.stem: The TROPIC OF CANCER passes through how many Indian STATES?
questions.explanation: Tropic of Cancer (23°26′ N) passes through 8 Indian states (west → east): Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, Mizoram. India is thus roughly half in the tropics, half in subtropics.

questions.stem: The latitude passing through India roughly through the CENTRAL part is:

options.option_text: Equator
Tropic of Cancer (23.5° N)
Arctic Circle
Tropic of Capricorn

questions.explanation: Tropic of Cancer — 23.5° N — passes through the middle of India. Equator (0°) is south of India (closest point Indira Point in Nicobar at ~6°N). Tropic of Capricorn is south of equator; Arctic Circle (66.5° N) far north.

questions.stem: The INDIAN STANDARD TIME (IST) is based on the meridian at:
questions.explanation: IST = GMT + 5:30 hours, referenced to 82.5° E longitude (passes through Mirzapur / Naini near Allahabad, UP). This 'standard meridian' gives a single national time. India is ~30° wide east-west so single time zone causes sun-time differences of ~2 hours end-to-end. passing through Mirzapur, UP.

questions.stem: The EQUATOR divides the Earth into:

options.option_text: Eastern and Western hemispheres
Northern and Southern hemispheres
Arctic and Antarctic
Old and New Worlds

questions.explanation: Equator (0° latitude) — divides Earth into Northern and Southern hemispheres. The Prime Meridian (0° longitude through Greenwich) + International Date Line (~180°) divide Eastern and Western hemispheres. Equator is ~40,075 km long.

questions.stem: The WORLD has how many STANDARD TIME ZONES?
questions.explanation: 24 main time zones (360°/15° each = 24, since Earth rotates 360° in 24 hr → 15°/hour). Some countries use half-hour / 45-min offsets (India = +5:30; Nepal = +5:45; Iran = +3:30). Russia: 11 zones. China: single zone despite wide longitude.

questions.stem: The INTERNATIONAL DATE LINE is approximately along:

options.option_text: 0° longitude
180° longitude

questions.explanation: IDL — roughly 180° meridian, zig-zagging to keep island groups and countries on the same calendar date (Kiribati line, Chukotka). Cross IDL going east → lose a day. Going west → gain a day. with kinks to avoid splitting countries.

questions.stem: India's SOUTHERNMOST point (mainland) is CAPE COMORIN / KANYAKUMARI. The southernmost point of India's TERRITORY is:

options.option_text: Kanyakumari
Indira Point, Great Nicobar Island
Rameshwaram
Dhanushkodi

questions.explanation: Indira Point (Great Nicobar) — 6°45′ N — southernmost point of Indian territory. Was called 'Pygmalion Point' earlier; renamed in honour of Indira Gandhi. Submerged permanently by 2004 tsunami. Kanyakumari is southernmost point of MAINLAND (8°4′ N).

questions.stem: If the longitude difference between two places is 60°, the local time difference between them is:

options.option_text: 2 hours, as every 30° equals one hour of time
4 hours, as every 15° equals one hour of time
6 hours, as every 10° equals one hour of time
3 hours, as every 20° equals one hour of time

questions.explanation: Earth rotates 360° in 24 hours, so it covers 15° every hour (360/24 = 15). A 60° difference therefore equals 60/15 = 4 hours. Option A is wrong because 30°/hr would mean Earth rotates only 720° in 24 hours — double the actual rate.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly identifies the POLEWARD boundary of the North Temperate Zone?

options.option_text: The Arctic Circle, situated at latitude 66.5°N
The Tropic of Cancer, situated at latitude 23.5°N
The Antarctic Circle, situated at latitude 66.5°S
The Prime Meridian, which runs at 0° longitude

questions.explanation: The North Temperate Zone lies between the Tropic of Cancer (23.5°N) and the Arctic Circle (66.5°N). The Arctic Circle is its poleward (upper) boundary. Option B — the Tropic of Cancer — is actually the equatorward boundary of the Temperate Zone, a common confusion in exams. Option D confuses longitude with latitude.

questions.stem: The 82°30'E meridian, used as the basis for Indian Standard Time, passes closest to which city in Uttar Pradesh?

options.option_text: Lucknow, the state capital of Uttar Pradesh
Mirzapur, a district near the Vindhya plateau
Varanasi, a major pilgrimage city on the Ganga
Kanpur, an industrial city on the Ganga river

questions.explanation: Mirzapur (approx. 82.6°E) lies nearest to the 82°30'E standard meridian and its clock tower is the traditional IST reference. Varanasi lies further east at ~83°E, making it the most tempting wrong answer since both cities are in eastern UP. Lucknow (~81°E) and Kanpur (~80.3°E) are too far west.

questions.stem: At a location of 120°E longitude, the local time is 6:00 AM. At the same instant, what is the local solar time at a place located at 75°E longitude?

options.option_text: 3:00 AM, as 75°E is exactly 3 hours behind 120°E
9:00 AM, as 75°E is exactly 3 hours ahead of 120°E
6:00 AM, as both places share the same calendar date
12:00 noon, as the longitude gap converts to 6 hours

questions.explanation: The difference is 120° − 75° = 45°. At 15° per hour, that equals 3 hours. Since 75°E is to the WEST of 120°E, it is 3 hours BEHIND: 6:00 AM − 3 hours = 3:00 AM. Option B is the classic reversal error — students confuse which meridian is ahead. Option D incorrectly divides 45° by 7.5 instead of 15.

questions.stem: The Tropic of Capricorn (23.5°S) passes through which of the following sets of continents?

options.option_text: South America, Africa, Australia, and mainland Asia
South America, Africa, and Australia only
Africa, Australia, and Antarctica only
South America, Africa, Australia, and Europe

questions.explanation: The Tropic of Capricorn crosses South America (Brazil, Argentina, Chile), Africa (Namibia, Botswana, South Africa, Mozambique), and Australia — exactly three continents. Asia's southernmost mainland point (~1°N) is in the Northern Hemisphere, so Option A is wrong. Antarctica lies between 66.5°S–90°S, well south of 23.5°S. Europe is entirely in the Northern Hemisphere.

questions.stem: The International Date Line bends sharply EASTWARD around the Republic of Kiribati, placing all its islands west of the line. What is the PRIMARY reason for this deviation?

options.option_text: To keep all of Kiribati's island groups on the same calendar date
To maintain standard 15° spacing between adjacent Pacific time zones
To align the Date Line precisely with the 180° meridian in that region
To prevent the Date Line from bisecting any exclusive economic zone

questions.explanation: In 1995, Kiribati unilaterally shifted the Date Line eastward so that its eastern islands (Line Islands, including Kiritimati) share the same calendar day as its western islands. Previously, the western and eastern islands were two calendar days apart, creating administrative and economic problems. Option D is plausible but wrong — the IDL crosses many EEZs; the Kiribati case was purely about calendar unity for a sovereign state.

questions.stem: City X is at 75°E longitude and City Y is at 105°W longitude. If it is 3:00 PM on Wednesday at City X, what is the local time and day at City Y?

options.option_text: 3:00 AM on Wednesday, the very same calendar day
3:00 AM on Thursday, the next calendar day forward
11:00 PM on Tuesday, the previous calendar day
3:00 PM on Thursday, exactly one full day later

questions.explanation: Step 1 — UTC offsets: 75°E → UTC+5 (75÷15=5); 105°W → UTC−7 (105÷15=7). Step 2 — Convert X to UTC: 3:00 PM − 5 h = 10:00 AM UTC Wednesday. Step 3 — Convert UTC to Y: 10:00 AM − 7 h = 3:00 AM Wednesday. No date change occurs because neither conversion crosses midnight. Option B (Thursday) is the most common error — students assume crossing large longitudes always changes the date, which is only true at the International Date Line (≈180°).
